title: $H-T$ Phase diagram of CeRh$_{2}$As$_{2}$: Refinement of the parity-switch scenario
authors: Changhee Lee, P. M. R. Brydon
abstract: The superconductivity of CeRh$_2$As$_2$ has drawn attention due to its first-order transition in magnetic fields. At first glance, the multiple superconducting (SC) phases as well as the first-order transition appear consistent with the parity-switch scenario, which emphasizes the role of strong Rashba spin-orbit coupling enabled by the locally non-centrosymmetric crystal structure. However, experimental phase diagrams exhibit notable deviations from this simple picture: thermodynamic measurements reveal a nearly vertical phase boundary of the high-field SC phase despite the orbital depairing effect, while transport measurements show that the initial slope of the high-field SC phase is steeper than that of the low-field SC phase. Here, we show that these discrepancies can be understood by considering the combined effects of nonsymmorphic band structure and coexisting antiferromagnetic order. We demonstrate that the symmetry-enforced electronic structure around the Dirac node and type-II Van Hove saddle points near the X point in the Brillouin zone boundary becomes more anisotropic with increased interlayer hopping amplitude, and this anisotropic band structure naturally accounts for the anomalous initial slope of the odd-parity SC phase. Meanwhile, a phenomenological theory incorporating coexisting antiferromagnetism explains the nearly vertical thermodynamic phase boundary as a consequence of field-enhanced odd-parity superconductivity enabled by the over-suppression of Pauli depairing.
summary: This paper refines the understanding of superconductivity in CeRh2As2 by addressing conflicts between theory and experiment regarding its H-T phase diagram. The authors demonstrate that complex electronic structure effects, arising from nonsymmorphic symmetries and coexisting antiferromagnetism, are necessary to explain anomalous superconducting behavior observed under magnetic fields.
main_problem: The study aims to reconcile experimental discrepancies in the H-T phase diagram of CeRh2As2—specifically the anomalous initial slope and nearly vertical boundary—with the simple parity-switch superconducting scenario.
main_result: The authors show that incorporating anisotropic band structure due to nonsymmorphic symmetries explains the steep odd-parity SC slope, while coexisting antiferromagnetism accounts for the near-vertical thermodynamic phase boundary via Pauli depairing suppression.
method: The work combines theoretical modeling using a 2D k.p Hamiltonian and Landau free energy formalism with analysis of experimental data from specific heat and resistivity measurements.
model_or_system: The system is the heavy fermion superconductor CeRh2As2, analyzed near the X point in the Brillouin zone boundary using a k.p Hamiltonian that incorporates interlayer hopping and Rashba SOC effects.
key_observables: H-T phase boundaries for SC and AFM phases; initial slopes of odd/even parity superconducting states ($	ext{oSC}$ vs $	ext{eSC}$).
important_parameters: Interlayer hopping amplitude ($t_\perp$), Rashba SOC parameters ($\alpha_x, \alpha_y$), magnetic field ($H$), and temperature ($T$).
main_assumptions: The standard Ginzburg-Landau theory is insufficient at high fields; the analysis relies on modeling the interplay between SC and AFM orders.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematic H-T phase diagrams showing first-order transitions, and Fermi surface plots highlighting Van Hove saddle points around the X point.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying experimental inconsistencies with simple models to developing a sophisticated theoretical framework involving anisotropic band structure calculations (k.p model) and phenomenological Landau theory incorporating coexisting AFM order.
why_interesting: While focused on heavy fermions, the detailed analysis of symmetry-enforced electronic structure near singularities (Dirac nodes/VHSs) and the interplay between magnetic ordering and superconductivity provides rich theoretical material relevant to strongly correlated quantum materials research.
